references.text: Isaac's blessing of Jacob is an example of patriarchal blessing that is passed down through generations, as seen here when Jacob blesses Ephraim and Manasseh.
The context of the blessing: Jacob crosses his hands and places Ephraim before Manasseh, even though Manasseh is the firstborn – a fact confirmed in verse 20.
Jacob's blessing of Joseph, father of Ephraim and Manasseh, continues the theme of blessing from chapter 48.
Moses' blessing of the tribe of Joseph mentions Ephraim and Manasseh and affirms Ephraim's precedence, in line with Jacob's blessing.

In Ruth 4:11 a similar blessing formula is used where Israel blesses by comparing to forebears (Rachel and Leah), just as Genesis 48:20 describes that Israel should bless by saying 'God make you like Ephraim and Manasseh'.
The verse describes the physical action that made possible the theological shift in which Ephraim was placed before Manasseh.
Ezekiel uses Ephraim's identity (established in Gen 48) as a symbol of the northern kingdom's reunification with Judah.
The verse explains the name 'Ephraim', which is central to the blessing formula and the ranking in the source verse.
